# `glue`

the two hemispheres of a cortex glued by a bridge after exactly their medial walls are cut, a derived manifold stored with its hemispheres labelling (left, right, bridge).

Version 2, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run glue --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run glue --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run glue --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex_pial [--hemispheres Structures] [--left "Cortex L"] [--right "Cortex R"]
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$surface"} (name the two-hemisphere surface (--surface)) | yes |
| `hemispheres` | selection set, manifold surface.manifold.0, where {"name": "$hemispheres"} (the original's hemisphere labelling, by name (--hemispheres; Brainstorm's `Structures`)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface` | `--surface` | none | - |  | the two-hemisphere surface, by name |
| `hemispheres` | `--hemispheres` | `Structures` | - |  | the original's hemisphere labelling, by name (default: Brainstorm's scout atlas Structures, the reference's) |
| `left` | `--left` | `Cortex L` | - |  | the labelling's entry that is the left hemisphere (default: Brainstorm's name) |
| `right` | `--right` | `Cortex R` | - |  | the labelling's entry that is the right hemisphere (default: Brainstorm's name) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{surface}_glued` | - |  | the glued surface's name |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`geometry.glue`](../nodes.md) | surface=surface, hemispheres=hemispheres | left=$left, right=$right | glued, labels |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `glued` | kind manifold, type surface, name $name, derived_from surface.manifold.0 |
| `labels` | kind selection, type partition, name {name}_hemispheres, on glued |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE GLUED CORTEX: the two hemispheres joined by the corpus callosum's bridge, a DERIVED manifold made by its own definition (a `make` move). The imported two-hemisphere mesh stays the manifold of
record (atlases, kernels, exports, results, figures); the glued surface is the default COMPUTATIONAL manifold for spatiotemporal pattern analysis (patterns cross hemispheres smoothly: one cortex), and results are
reported back on the original two hemispheres.

The hemispheres are READ, never found: the caller names the original's HEMISPHERE LABELLING (`--hemispheres`; Brainstorm's scout atlas `Structures` by default, its entries `Cortex L`, `Cortex R` and
`unassigned`: the reference's names, the defaults of `--left` and `--right`). A labelling whose left or right member is not one connected piece, that leaves cortex outside its own `unassigned`, or that
puts a face in both hemispheres is refused with the reason. The medial wall is the Desikan-Killiany atlas' `unassigned`, as before.

Stored, as an atlas is (Selections, no index field):
  {name}                  the glued surface: every vertex of the original off the medial wall, in ascending order, then the bridge's
  {name}_hemispheres      ONE labelling of the glued surface: the input labelling's entries (names, codes, colours) and one more, `bridge`; every glued vertex a member of one
The cut removes EXACTLY the medial wall (its vertices and the faces touching them, nothing more), so the correspondence glued -> original needs nothing stored: the labelling's non-bridge vertices,
in order, are the original's vertices off the wall, in order. A wall whose exact cut cannot be bridged (several pieces, several rim loops, cortex enclosed by it) is refused with the reason.
Transfers: original -> glued (values copied; the bridge by sourcesOf interpolation; the medial wall has no counterpart) and glued -> original (exact; the bridge dropped like the medial wall); atlases are
carried by `transfer`. `eigenmodes` and `apply_kernel` take this surface BY NAME. A glue stored in an earlier form (a map field and a bridge selection, or a `{name}_kept` selection) is converted in place by `nxr-neuro migrate glue`, which
refuses a glue that removed more than the medial wall (re-run glue).

What it cannot resolve: the pieces must match by anatomy (exactly the medial walls cut, a bridge grown); a pair that does not match is refused with the reason. The bridge is a construction, not cortex.

  nxr-neuro run glue --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex_pial [--hemispheres Structures] [--left "Cortex L"] [--right "Cortex R"]
```
